<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Plan 075 gave `harness commit` a fourth branch (`ingress-unverified`, the Windows named pipe) and updated the instructions page to describe it. It did NOT update the managed `AGENTS.md` block, which still promises exactly two outcomes: a confirmed note, or a named buffer plus the nudge that drains it. On Windows an agent is therefore told to expect an outcome it cannot get, and is pointed at a recovery command that refuses on that platform.

The text fix is one paragraph. The DEFECT is that the outcome contract exists in two hand-maintained prose copies with nothing forcing them to agree — so it drifted once and will drift again at the next branch change. This plan converges both surfaces on one `CommitMode`-keyed table over a companion outcome map, so a fifth mode cannot be added without the guidance failing to compile. That is the house pattern already proven twice: `TRACE2_TARGET_POLICY` (ingress.ts) and `RETAINED_FIELD_RENDERING` (nudge.ts).

This is the same failure this family of plans exists to kill — a surface claiming more than the code delivers — reappearing one layer up, in the documentation OF the safeguard. It kept reappearing during the build, too: four review rounds each found one more single-ownership claim (a comment, an acceptance criterion, a doc comment above the table itself) that one hand-written exception falsified. The lesson is recorded as D5: before asserting "X is the only writer of Y", grep for Y.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- The managed block names every outcome an agent can actually receive from `harness commit`, including the named-pipe path where attribution is unverified and the nudge must NOT be run.
- The outcome contract lives in ONE place: a table keyed by `CommitMode` declaring which outcome each mode yields, over a companion map declaring each outcome's promise and recovery exactly once. Both guidance surfaces render from it, and the how-doc points at it rather than restating it — no second hand-maintained prose copy of the outcome list anywhere.
- Adding a fifth `CommitMode` is a COMPILE ERROR at the guidance table, not a review catch. A guarantee about future code needs the type system, not a test (DL-007) — and the guarantee is bounded: the compiler forces a new mode to be DESCRIBED, while whether it was described CORRECTLY is carried by the renderer owning every mention of the recovery verb, the shared-outcome-object design, and tests.
- Repos carrying the old block migrate gracefully: it reads as `stale`, doctor warns, and `harness instructions commit --inject` refreshes it in place.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Changing commit BEHAVIOUR. Not one branch of `commit-service.ts` moves; this plan changes what the guidance SAYS about branches that already exist.
- Windows replay support. Still blocked on the unverified transport premise — nobody has run `git config --global --get trace2.eventTarget` on a Windows box.
- Editing `AGENTS.md` outside the managed markers, in this repo or any other. The block owns the region between its fences and nothing else.
- A `windows-latest` CI leg. Approved by prime, but it belongs to issue #108's PR under that ruling's same-PR-and-green condition — not here.
- Rewording the instructions page's prose beyond what deriving it from the table requires.
